title: Outside the temple gate
body: Tao Ying takes her son Xiao Ye to a big temple on a complimentary ticket, believing that children under 110 centimetres need none. At the gate, a young guard in red insists the boy is taller than the red line on the wall, which looks like an earthworm. When Xiao Ye is made to stand against it, the line reaches only his ear. The crowd jeers, and the guard accuses Tao Ying of trying to sneak in an extra person and demands that she apologise and buy a valid ticket. For her son's sake she decides to swallow her pride and buy one, but Xiao Ye asks, full of surprise, 'Mama, did you really not buy a ticket?' The look on his face frightens her: if she buys the ticket now, she can never explain herself to him. She pulls him away to the park, but the boy has fallen silent and sullen. The narrator remarks: 'Xiao Ye has suddenly grown up.'
